editorial.titleTr: Strong Winds of Change: Personnel Shake-up Signals Broader Governmental Overhaul
summaryTr: Presidential Chief of Staff Kang Hoon-sik has submitted his resignation over personnel failures.
The withdrawal of candidates Kim Seung-won and Yong Hye-in has exposed loopholes in the vetting system.
The government must dispel allegations of behind-the-scenes interference and overhaul state affairs across the board.
editorial.bodyTr: Personnel failures and declining approval ratings prompted presidential Chief of Staff Kang Hoon-sik to announce his resignation on the 21st. The withdrawals of candidates Kim Seung-won and Yong Hye-in exposed verification lapses, necessitating a review and overhaul of the administration's personnel and civil affairs operations. As suspicions grow that unofficial advisors are influencing personnel decisions and controversies over the government's response mount, the administration must comprehensively review its overall state affairs operations.

editorials.titleTr: Presidential Visit to US Must Break Through Stalled Bilateral Relations
summaryTr: President Lee Jae-myung should resolve pending Korea-U.S. issues through a summit with Trump during the UN General Assembly.
A top-level decision is essential as the two countries' positions diverge significantly on Hormuz Strait cooperation and the $350 billion investment plan.
If the summit falls through due to unclear scheduling, concerns over the instability of the Korea-U.S. alliance could deepen.
editorials.bodyTr: President Lee Jae-myung should use his attendance at the United Nations General Assembly as an opportunity to resolve pending Korean-American issues through a summit with Trump. Given the widening gap between the two countries' positions on cooperation in the Strait of Hormuz and South Korea's 350 billion dollar investment in the United States, a decision-making meeting between the two leaders will be necessary. With the schedule for the Korea-U.S. summit remaining unclear, concerns about alliance instability could grow if the talks fall short on time or fail to materialize altogether.

summaryTr: Five key military commanders in the Dec. 12-3 martial law crisis sentenced to heavy prison terms of 9 to 18 years
Court emphasizes duty to uphold constitution takes precedence over following orders from superiors
Concerns over serious aftereffects including military command vacuum and plummeting morale

The ruling has raised social concerns that serious aftereffects will occur, including security gaps from the large-scale departure of military leadership and declining morale within the armed forces.

editorial.title: [사설] 인사 실패, 왜 아무도 책임지지 않나
editorial.body: 입력 김승원 법무부 장관 후보자의 사퇴는 이재명 정부의 대표적인 인사 실패로 기록되고 있다. 후보자 지명과 사퇴까지 모든 과정에서 청와대와 정부·여당의 인사 시스템은 먹통이었다. 청와대의 검증은 무능했고, 더불어민주당의 청문회는 무책임했다. 검증의 기본인 신약 로비 의혹 기소유예 사건은 국민 눈높이의 공정에는 한참 못 미치는 과오인데도 전혀 걸러지지 않았다. 김민석 민주당 대표는 “볼수록 잘된 인사”라고 옹호하기에 바빴다. 국민 입장에선 김 후보자가 대통령 공소취소 모임 대표를 지냈기에 특혜를 누린다고 의심할 수밖에 없었다. 민주당은 대통령 기자회견(18일) 하루 전 인사청문경과보고서 채택을 강행하며 민심과 더 멀어졌다. 결국 이 대통령이 “국민의 눈높이를 고려하겠다”는 신중론을 내비쳤고, 이튿날 김 후보자가 사퇴했다. 말끝마다 강조하는 ‘국민의 눈높이’가 왜 인사 검증에는 전혀 작동하지 않는지 답답하기만 하다. 이 대통령은 기자회견에서 “인사 시스템을 재점검해보려 한다”고 했다. 2기 내각 6명의 장관 후보자 중 2명이 낙마하고 다른 후보자들도 각종 의혹에 휩싸인 상황으로 볼 때, 재점검 수준으로는 오류를 바로잡기 어려워 보인다. 인사 시스템과 담당자 모두 대대적인 쇄신이 필요하다. 김 후보자의 경우 사퇴 결정 이틀 전 추가 의혹에 대한 탄원서가 청와대에 전달됐다고 하니, 도대체 청와대는 검증하기는 한 것인지 의문이 든다. 앞서 낙마한 용혜인 후보자의 비례대표 국회의원 겸직도 국민이 분노하기 전에 당연히 점검했어야 할 문제였다. 이재명 정부 들어 1년3개월간 장관 5명이 낙마했다. 대통령이 인사에 담으려 했다는 여성·탕평·검찰 개혁 등의 메시지는 오간 데 없고 국민을 실망시키기만 했다. 이쯤 되면 인사 참사라 할 만하지만, 누구도 책임지지 않고 있다. 이 대통령의 편협한 인재 풀이 일차적 문제겠으나 그런 인사들을 검증하는 시스템이 작동하지 않고 있는 것은 보다 심각한 문제다. 김현지·정진상 등 이 대통령의 성남 라인 측근이 인사 때마다 거론되면서 공적 인사 시스템에 대한 불신만 커지고 있다. 청와대 인사위원장인 강훈식 대통령비서실장을 포함해 인사 시스템 전반을 제대로 점검하고 합당한 책임을 물리는 조치가 따라야 한다. 검증 역할을 한 야당 의원을 적대시하고 남 탓을 하는 행태도 멈춰야 한다. 이 대통령은 지지율 하락의 원인을 “국민에 대한 존중심 부족”에서 찾았다. 인사 실패의 원인 분석도 같은 인식이 필요해 보인다.

editorial.titleTr: [Editorial] Personnel Misstep: Why Is No One Taking Responsibility?
summaryTr: The withdrawal of the Justice Minister nominee exposed the incompetence of Lee Jae-myung's government's personnel system.
The presidential office's vetting failure and the Democratic Party's irresponsibility have only eroded public trust.
A complete overhaul of the personnel system is essential when no one takes responsibility.
editorial.bodyTr: The resignation of Justice Minister nominee Kim Seung-won is being recorded as a representative personnel failure of the Lee Jae-myung administration. Throughout the entire process from nomination to withdrawal, the personnel systems of the presidential office, government, and ruling party proved completely dysfunctional. The presidential office's vetting was incompetent, and the Democratic Party's confirmation hearing was irresponsible. The Shin Yak lobbying allegations and prosecutorial suspension case, which should have been basic vetting criteria, fell far short of public standards for fairness, yet were not filtered out at all. Democratic Party leader Kim Min-seok was busy defending it as "a personnel move that looks better the more you examine it." From the public's perspective, it was unavoidable to suspect that nominee Kim received preferential treatment because he had served as chairman of a group supporting the president's dismissal of prosecution. The Democratic Party rushed adoption of the personnel hearing report one day before the president's press conference on the 18th, distancing itself further from public sentiment. Eventually, the president suggested a cautious approach, saying he would "consider the public's expectations," and the next day nominee Kim withdrew. It is only frustrating why the "public's expectations" that he constantly emphasizes does not apply at all to personnel vetting. At the press conference, the president said he would "reexamine the personnel system." Given that two of six cabinet minister nominees for the second term have fallen and other nominees are embroiled in various allegations, it appears that a simple reexamination will be insufficient to correct these errors. A comprehensive overhaul is needed in both the personnel system and those responsible for it. In Kim's case, a petition regarding additional allegations was reportedly delivered to the presidential office two days before his withdrawal decision, raising questions about whether the presidential office conducted any vetting at all. The dual position as proportional representative and National Assembly member held by previously fallen nominee Yong Hye-in should have been routinely checked before the public became angry about it. Over the past one year and three months of the Lee administration, five ministers have fallen. The messages the president tried to convey through personnel appointments regarding women, balanced appointments, and prosecutorial reform have vanished without a trace, only disappointing the nation. At this point, one might call it a personnel catastrophe, yet no one is taking responsibility. The president's narrow talent pool is a primary issue, but more critically, the system to vet such personnel is not functioning. As the president's Seongnam circle associates like Kim Hyun-ji and Jung Jin-sang are repeatedly cited in each personnel appointment, distrust in the public personnel system only grows. A thorough examination of the overall personnel system, including Kang Hoon-sik, the presidential chief of staff and chair of the presidential personnel committee, must be followed by appropriate accountability measures. The administration must also stop its hostile treatment of opposition lawmakers who played a vetting role and stop blaming others. The president attributed his declining approval ratings to a "lack of respect for the people." The analysis of the cause of personnel failures appears to require the same awareness.

editorial.title: A risky opening
editorial.body: Government supportive of bill to ease controls on contacts with N. Koreans The government is reportedly supportive of a bill that would allow South Koreans seeking to contact North Korean residents to do so by simply giving prior notice to the government, rather than obtaining its prior approval. The bill in question to revise the Inter-Korean Exchange and Cooperation Act was proposed by Rep. Kim Joon-hyung of the minor Rebuilding Korea Party in June last year. Under the current law, the Minister of Unification may reject an application for prior approval of contact with North Korean residents if there is a clear concern that the contact could undermine national security or the maintenance of public order. The revision bill would eliminate discretionary authority to reject applications and instead require only the submission of a report on the outcome after the contact. Since the government supports the revision bill, if the ruling Democratic Party of Korea, which holds a majority in the National Assembly, pushes it through, the bill will pass. If the bill passes, civilian contact with North Korea will be fully permitted for the first time in 36 years since the law was enacted. The public is uneasy about this. That is because, if handled carelessly, it could have the self-defeating effect of creating even greater gaps in national security. The government's position is seen as a strategic move to improve inter-Korean relations in the future. How wonderful it would be if South and North Korean civilians could increase genuine exchanges as the government hopes. But the reality will be quite the opposite. Given the nature of the North Korean regime, it is highly unlikely that North Korean residents who meet South Korean residents would be ordinary civilians. They are likely to be North Korean agents or informants conducting operations against South Korea. North Korea defines inter-Korean relations as those between "two hostile states" and is building barriers and barbed-wire fences and laying mines along the Military Demarcation Line. In July, Pyongyang announced it would expand and strengthen the functions and missions of the General Bureau of Reconnaissance Intelligence, which collects intelligence and conducts clandestine operations abroad. While North Korea is becoming increasingly overt in targeting South Korea, South Korea alone appears intent on throwing open the door. There is also a possibility that some South Koreans may seek contact with North Koreans for ulterior purposes. In September last year, the Supreme Court upheld the convictions of two former executives of the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions who had been indicted on charges of secretly contacting North Korean agents overseas and carrying out their instructions at home. This happened even under the current law requiring prior government approval. What, then, would happen if South Koreans were allowed to contact North Koreans freely without prior approval, simply by notifying the government in advance? If the bill in question passes, there are also growing concerns that it could be exploited for North Korean operations targeting South Korea or that illicit remittances to North Korea could proliferate. summaryTr: 남한 정부가 북한과의 민간인 접촉 제한을 완화하는 법안을 지지하고 있으며, 사전 승인 대신 신고만 요구하도록 하고 있다.
비평가들은 북한 접촉자들이 일반 민간인이 아니라 요원일 가능성이 높기 때문에 이러한 변화가 간첩 활동과 보안 위반의 위험을 초래할 수 있다고 경고하고 있다.

editorial.bodyTr:
정부, 북한주민 접촉 규제 완화 법안 지지

정부가 북한주민과 접촉하려는 남한 국민들이 정부 사전 승인을 받는 대신 단순히 사전 통보만으로 접촉할 수 있도록 허용하는 법안을 지지하고 있는 것으로 알려졌다. 지난해 6월 소수당 국민의힘 산하 재건신당 김준형 의원이 제안한 '남북교류협력법' 개정안이 바로 그것이다. 현행법에 따르면 통일부 장관은 북한주민과의 접촉이 국가안보나 공공질서 유지를 심각하게 해칠 우려가 있으면 사전 승인 신청을 거부할 수 있다. 개정안은 신청 거부 재량권을 폐지하고 접촉 이후 결과 보고서 제출만을 요구하는 것으로 변경하려고 한다.

정부가 개정안을 지지하고 있기 때문에 국회 다수당인 더불어민주당이 이를 추진하면 통과될 가능성이 높다. 법안이 통과되면 1988년 법 제정 이후 36년 만에 민간인의 북한 접촉이 완전히 허용되는 것이다. 국민들이 불안해하는 이유가 여기 있다. 부주의하게 다루면 오히려 국가안보에 더 큰 허점을 만드는 역효과를 초래할 수 있기 때문이다.

정부의 입장은 향후 남북관계 개선을 위한 전략적 움직임으로 보인다. 정부가 바라는 대로 남북 민간인이 진정한 교류를 늘릴 수 있다면 얼마나 좋을까. 그러나 현실은 정반대일 가능성이 높다. 북한 체제의 특성상 남한 국민과 만나는 북한주민은 일반 시민이 아닐 가능성이 매우 크다. 북한 대남 공작을 벌이는 북한 간첩이거나 협력자일 가능성이 높다. 북한은 남북관계를 "두 적대국가 간의 관계"로 정의하고 군사분계선 일대에 장벽과 철조망을 세우고 지뢰를 매설하고 있다. 7월 평양은 대외 정보수집과 비밀공작을 벌이는 정찰국의 기능과 역할을 확대하고 강화하겠다고 선언했다.

북한이 대남 공작을 점점 더 노골화하고 있는 반면, 남한만 홀로 문을 활짝 열려고 한다. 또한 일부 남한 국민들이 불순한 목적으로 북한주민과의 접촉을 추구할 가능성도 있다. 지난해 9월 대법원은 해외에서 북한 간첩과 비밀리에 접촉해 그들의 지시를 국내에서 수행한 혐의로 기소된 민주노총 전 간부 2명의 유죄를 확정했다. 이는 정부 사전 승인을 요구하는 현행법 체계 아래에서도 발생했다. 그렇다면 남한 국민이 정부 사전 승인 없이 단순 사전 통보만으로 북한주민과 자유롭게 접촉할 수 있게 된다면 어떻게 될까?

법안이 통과되면 북한의 대남 공작에 악용되거나 대북 송금이 급증할 우려도 커진다. 더불어민주당이 추진한 입법으로 국정원의 북한 간첩 수사권이 2024년 경찰로 완전히 이관된 이후 국내 북한 간첩 적발 및 수사 능력이 크게 약화됐다. 이준석 행정부 때 국방부 산하 군 보안 기구인 국방부 방첩사령부마저 해체됐으며, 그 기능들이 여러 기관에 분산됐다. 이러한 허점들이 해소될 때까지 남북교류 규제를 완화할 필요가 없다. 북한은 남한에 대한 적대성을 점점 더 노골화하며 문을 굳게 닫고 있다. 지금은 민간교류의 문을 성급하게 활짝 열 때가 아니라 해체된 방첩 네트워크를 복구하고 국가 안보 태세를 한층 강화할 때다. 이 정부와 여당은 국민의 우려의 목소리에 귀를 기울여야 한다.

Koreans The government is reportedly supportive of a bill that would allow South Koreans seeking to contact North Korean residents to do so by simply giving prior notice to the government, rather than obtaining its prior approval. If the bill passes, civilian contact with North Korea will be fully permitted for the first time in 36 years since the law was enacted. The public is uneasy about this. That is because, if handled carelessly, it could have the self-defeating effect of creating even greater gaps in national security. The government's position is seen as a strategic move to improve inter-Korean relations in the future. How wonderful it would be if South and North Korean civilians could increase genuine exchanges as the government hopes. But the reality will be quite the opposite. Given the nature of the North Korean regime, it is highly unlikely that North Korean residents who meet South Korean residents would be ordinary civilians. They are likely to be North Korean agents or informants conducting operations against South Korea. North Korea defines inter-Korean relations as those between "two hostile states" and is building barriers and barbed-wire fences and laying mines along the Military Demarcation Line. In July, Pyongyang announced it would expand and strengthen the functions and missions of the General Bureau of Reconnaissance Intelligence, which collects intelligence and conducts clandestine operations abroad. While North Korea is becoming increasingly overt in targeting South Korea, South Korea alone appears intent on throwing open the door. There is also a possibility that some South Koreans may seek contact with North Koreans for ulterior purposes. In September last year, the Supreme Court upheld the convictions of two former executives of the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions who had been indicted on charges of secretly contacting North Korean agents overseas and carrying out their instructions at home. This happened even under the current law requiring prior government approval. Even the Defense Counterintelligence Command, the military’s counterintelligence organization, was dismantled under the Lee Jae Myung administration, after which its functions were dispersed among multiple organizations. editorials.titleTr: Editorial: With Criminal Justice Overhaul Imminent, Top Posts Sit Empty—Isn't That a Problem?
summaryTr: Next month on the 2nd, a historic transformation of the criminal justice system begins for the first time in 70 years.
The four key leadership positions—prosecutor general, justice minister, head of the Serious Crimes Division, and police commissioner—are all vacant.
With the criminal justice system overhaul looming, the leadership vacuum poses a serious problem.
editorials.bodyTr: Next month on the 2nd, a new Criminal Procedure Act separating investigation and prosecution will be implemented, and with the launch of the Prosecution Service and the Serious Crimes Investigation Agency, Korea's criminal justice system will undergo a major transformation for the first time in over 70 years. However, the positions of the heads of the four key institutions of the criminal justice system—the Justice Minister, the Prosecutor General, the chief of the Serious Crimes Investigation Agency, and the Police Commissioner—remain vacant.

summary: 38년 만에 불법 농지가 합법화되는 조치가 추진 중이다.
정부는 현실에 맞춘 근본적인 개혁이 필요하다고 지적했다.
임시방편이 아닌 체계적인 해결책이 요구된다.
editorial.stance: 농지 불법 거래의 근본적 해결을 위해 현실 기반의 정책 개혁이 필수적이다
editorial.titleTr: [Editorial] Legalizing 'Illegal Farmland' After 38 Years...Time for Real Fix, Not a Band-Aid
summaryTr: A measure to legalize illegal farmland is being pushed forward for the first time in 38 years.
The government pointed out that fundamental reform tailored to reality is necessary.
A systematic solution, not a temporary fix, is required.
